standard.title: Interpret and analyse texts with cultural and critical awareness
standard.description: interpret and analyse information, ideas and opinions in a range of spoken, written and multimodal texts, and respond appropriately to cultural context, purpose and audience
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can locate and process information in texts analytically and respond for purpose and audience (AC9LCH6C03). They can analyse perspective and language variation. They have not yet evaluated credibility of sources, analysed humour and cultural reference, identified register variation across formal and informal contexts, or responded with empathetic or critical personal stances.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students interpret and analyse information, ideas and opinions in a range of spoken, written and multimodal texts — evaluating credibility, analysing cultural reference and humour, and responding appropriately to cultural context, purpose and audience.

nodes.label: Source credibility and critical information evaluation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate the credibility of information sources in the target language and apply strategies to assess and compare information across sources.
nodes.minimum_width: Evaluate the credibility of at least two target language sources using at least two criteria, and explain which is more reliable for a given purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Use target language digital and print sources to research topics; evaluate source credibility using appropriate criteria; compare information across sources; use target language search tools; distinguish between fact, opinion and interpretation in informative texts.
wider: Research a contested topic using target language sources — compare how different sources frame the same information, evaluate their credibility, and present a synthesis that acknowledges source differences
Investigate what makes a source credible in the target language information context — discuss whether credibility criteria differ across languages or communities
nodes.hinge_reason: Source credibility evaluation is the prerequisite for all analytical text work at Y7-8. Students who cannot evaluate sources cannot distinguish reliable from unreliable information — which undermines the quality and integrity of all analytical and research-based responses.

response_modes.reason: Source credibility evaluation requires students to apply explicit criteria — not just judge intuitively. Explicit instruction on credibility criteria (author, currency, purpose, evidence) followed by comparative source analysis tasks builds the systematic evaluative capacity.

success_criteria: Evaluates at least two target language sources using at least two explicit credibility criteria
Explains which source is more reliable for a given purpose and why

nodes.label: Analysing register, humour and cultural reference
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and analyse register variation, humour and culturally-embedded reference in target language texts, and discuss how these features serve the text's purpose.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two instances of register variation or cultural reference in a text and explain how each serves the text's purpose or audience.
nodes.typical_width: Identify register differences between formal and informal texts; analyse how humour works in target language media; identify cultural references that require background knowledge to interpret; compare target language humour with Australian expressions of humour; read imaginative texts and maintain a reading journal.
wider: Compare target language and English humour in equivalent media formats — identify what is shared and what is culturally specific, and discuss what the comparison reveals about cultural values
Analyse a culturally-embedded reference in a target language text — explain what background knowledge is needed to interpret it and discuss what happens when this knowledge is absent

response_modes.reason: Register, humour and cultural reference operate differently across text types and genres. Students who have analysed these features in only one genre cannot generalise their analytical strategies. Varied text type encounters build flexible analytical capacity.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background learners often understand cultural references and humour intuitively but have not examined why they work. Width investment here — making implicit cultural knowledge explicit and analytical — builds the explanatory capacity that distinguishes deep from surface cultural understanding.
success_criteria: Identifies at least two instances of register variation or cultural reference in a text
Explains how at least one of these features serves the text's purpose or audience

nodes.label: Responding with empathy and critical stance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can respond to imaginative and informative texts with empathy and critical awareness — demonstrating understanding of perspective, cultural context and authorial intention.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce at least one response to a text that demonstrates both empathy with a character or perspective and a critical observation about the text's cultural context or authorial choices.
nodes.typical_width: Respond to narratives with empathy — writing or performing from a character's perspective; identify differences in formal and informal register and replicate these in own responses; compare cultural expressions across texts; respond to First Nations Australian stories in English in target language.
wider: Write a response to a text that takes a critical stance — challenging an assumption, identifying a cultural bias, or questioning an authorial choice — with textual evidence
Compare responses to the same text across different readers or cultural perspectives — discuss how background knowledge and cultural positioning shape interpretation

response_modes.reason: Empathetic and critical response integrates source evaluation (node 1) and cultural reference analysis (node 2) into a full interpretive act. The teaching investment is in creating genuine reading and response conditions — real texts, real audiences — that require both engagement and critical distance.

success_criteria: Produces a response demonstrating empathy with a perspective or character
Includes at least one critical observation about cultural context or authorial choice with textual support
